sections.h2: Where in Bryan do Williams County deeds get filed?
sections.html:
Head to the second floor of the courthouse, One Courthouse Square, Bryan, OH 43506, or call 419-636-3259. The counter operates on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m. Filings must arrive by 4:00 p.m.

Staff keep a lasting record of every paper that transfers or encumbers land here, and indexing lets a searcher follow who held title and which debts attach. The county sits on the Ohio line with two other states: Hillsdale County, Michigan is to the north, and DeKalb and Steuben counties of Indiana are to the west. Fulton, Henry and Defiance counties complete the Ohio side. Bryan is the seat and the biggest city.

sections.h2: How much is recording a deed in Williams County?
sections.html:
Senate Bill 94 let counties add a $5.00 preservation surcharge under R.C. 317.32, and Williams County's Recorder applied it starting January 1, 2025. Reference fees and the standardization guidelines still apply on top.

Amounts taken from the Williams County Recorder's pages
ItemAmount
Recording, pages one and two$39.00
Each page after two$8.00
Reference fee$4.00
Paper that misses the format rules$20.00 added
Copy made at the counter$0.25 per page
Copy ordered in writing$2.00 per page

Certified copies follow the Ohio Revised Code schedule that the Recorder's fees page reproduces.

sections.h2: What layout does Ohio expect on a deed filed in Williams County?
sections.html:
R.C. 317.114 gives every recorder the same standard so that recording stamps have room on the page. A deed that falls short is still recorded, with $20 more collected. Here is what Williams County's Recorder asks for.

  • Dark blue or black ink only, and no highlighter.
  • A font of 10 points or larger.
  • One inch of white space left, right and bottom.
  • Page one keeps 3 inches clear at the top, later pages 1.5 inches.
  • Paper from letter size (8.5 by 11) to legal length (8.5 by 14).

Four categories escape the rules: documents signed before July 1, 2009, papers from a court or taxing authority, state and federal forms with DD214 discharges, and plats.

sections.h2: Which stamps does a Williams County deed need first?
sections.html:
A conveyance can arrive by mail only after the Engineer and the Auditor have stamped it, a rule that covers deeds, land contracts, easements and affidavits. The County Engineer reviews the legal description, the Auditor then names the conveyance charge, and for many documents the Treasurer first confirms that taxes on the parcel are paid.

  • Engineer: clears the legal description.
  • Treasurer: validates payment of taxes.
  • Auditor, 419-636-5639: states the charge.
  • Recorder: records and indexes the stamped deed.

The conveyance fee posted by the Auditor is $4 per $1,000 of price, with a transfer fee of $0.50 per parcel or deed. R.C. 319.202 assigns that fee to the grantor and requires the grantee's value statement. New conveyance standards started on January 1, 2026, and a link to them is on the Auditor's page.

sections.h2: What does Williams County look like in Census numbers?
sections.html:
The July 2025 estimate is 36,549 people, a 1.5 percent drop from the April 2020 base. QuickFacts counts 15,476 households in 16,659 housing units, and 76.3 percent of homes have owner occupants.

  • Value of the middle owner-held home: $150,000.
  • Middle owner outlay: $1,163 a month with a loan, $462 with none.
  • Middle gross rent: $791.
  • Middle household income: $61,048 (2024 dollars).
  • Residents past 65: 22.8 percent.
  • Permits pulled in 2025: 44.

Density is 88.2 residents per square mile across about 421 square miles of land. Census designated places include Alvordton, Kunkle, Lake Seneca, Nettle Lake and Pulaski.

sections.h2: How does someone obtain a copy of a Williams County deed?
sections.html:
Walk in, and the counter copy of a public record, a deed among them, is $0.25 per page, with staff glad to help find it. Written requests run $2.00 per page and need the volume and page from the Ohio Land Records index, a check or money order, and a stamped envelope addressed to you. Phone and email requests are not filled.

That online index covers filings from October 25, 1999 forward and shows new entries within a day of recording. It names the owner, document type and property description without displaying the document itself. Certified copies exist, though in person a plain copy costs the same $0.25 per page, so request a certified one only when a lender or court insists on it.

Plats are searchable through the County Engineer's site. The Ohio Recorders' Association also lists every county recorder along with the regulations and fees found in the Revised Code, which is handy for comparing what neighboring counties collect.

The Recorder has flagged a mailer called a "Deed Processing Notice" from a South Dakota company that asks homeowners for $83 to send a deed copy. Deeds are public records, so a friend can collect one for you at the courthouse.

sections.h2: What do Williams County's population and work patterns suggest about its housing market?
sections.html:
Population peaked at 39,188 in the 2000 census, then slipped to 37,642 in 2010 and 37,102 in 2020. In the Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, 61.0 percent of people aged 16 and up are in the civilian labor force and the average commute takes 19.8 minutes. The county had 802 employer establishments and 16,283 jobs in 2023, per the same source.

  • High school graduates among adults 25 and older: 91.8 percent.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 13.7 percent.
  • Households with broadband: 85.5 percent.
  • Veterans: 1,784.
  • Persons in poverty: 10.3 percent.

sections.h2: When was Williams County formed, and who oversees it?
sections.html:
Lawmakers created the county on April 1, 1820 and it was organized on February 2, 1824, with a name that honors David Williams, one of John Andre's captors in the Revolutionary War. Three commissioners oversee county departments. In total area it is the 53rd largest Ohio county, and its airport lies about two nautical miles east of downtown Bryan.

The Recorder holds documentation back to the start of land ownership in the county, though the online index begins in 1999, so older deeds need a trip to the courthouse.

sections.h2: Which other Williams County offices touch a house sale?
sections.html:
The county's Useful Links page maps the neighbors of the Recorder.

  • Probate Court: estates, guardianships and trusts, relevant when a house passes through an estate before sale.
  • Planning Commission handles zoning questions about lots and uses.
  • Records Center is the county repository for both public and confidential county records.
  • Clerk of Courts takes passports, divorce records and common pleas cases.
  • Property Fraud Alert: guidance posted for owners who worry about forged filings.

The Auditor, Engineer and Treasurer sit alongside these, and the Recorder is the last stop.

faqs.q: What time does the Williams County Recorder stop taking deeds?
faqs.a: At 4:00 p.m., half an hour before the office closes. The counter is upstairs in the Bryan courthouse and opens at 8:30 a.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: What will recording one Williams County deed cost?
faqs.a: Expect $39.00 for a deed of up to two pages, then $8.00 for every page beyond that, since the January 1, 2025 change. Reference fees of $4.00 may be added, and sloppy formatting brings a $20.00 penalty.

faqs.q: How is the Williams County conveyance fee figured?
faqs.a: The Auditor posts $4 per $1,000 of the purchase price, with $0.50 for each parcel or deed as the transfer fee. Ask the Auditor for the total on your price.

faqs.q: Does the Williams County Recorder accept deeds by mail?
faqs.a: Only when the Engineer and the Auditor have stamped the document beforehand. The same goes for land contracts, easements and affidavits.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to get my Williams County deed copy?
faqs.a: Stop by the Recorder's counter, where copies are a quarter a page. A mailed request costs $2.00 per page and must give the volume and page, with payment and a self addressed envelope.
